steps.text: Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat.
Mix together ground turkey, pesto, garlic, feta cheese, 1 1/2 teaspoons seasoned salt, and breadcrumbs in a bowl until evenly blended. Form into 4 patties.
Grill pesto burgers until no longer pink in the center, about 5 minutes per side. Sprinkle with seasoned salt halfway through cooking.

raw_recipe.headline: Pesto Turkey Burgers
raw_recipe.description: This Mediterranean-style turkey burger is flavored with basil pesto and crumbled feta cheese. It’s delicious, fancy, and ready in only 20 minutes! Serve on buns with lettuce and tomato.
raw_recipe.name: Pesto Turkey Burgers

review.reviewBody: Wow! These were the BEST turkey burgers I've ever had. To be honest, I was iffy about using a recipe that was new and didn't have a picture but I'm glad I did. I already had all of the ingedients in bulk (and thanks to Costco, it's actually fairly inexpensive for ingredients like Pesto and Feta cheese). I don't have an outdoor grill, but I baked them at about 400 for 10 minutes and then broiled them until they were browned (about 8 minutes). I toasted the buns and topped it with a sauce that I make which is equal parts mayo and dijon mustard mixed with about a teaspoon of fresh garlic and a dash of crushed red pepper. These are the best burgers I've ever had. Thank you SO much for this recipe!

Nice change from a traditional burger while remaining quick to assemble. I don't have a grill, so I baked these in the oven at 400 F for 11 mins total. I forgot to add the breadcrumbs (for which I was planning to substitute quinoa), but they stayed together just fine anyways. I thought they tasted a bit too salty, but I did make seasoning salt from scratch since I didn't have any pre-prepared, so my mix may have been off. Very tasty served with hummus, tomato, and spinach!

For those who can't have bread or are trying to eat low carb: I replaced the bread crumbs with silken tofu (different from regular tofu), which was a tip I found online from a chef's video...and it worked great! The burgers held together and were nice and moist. And then of course I ate them without buns and used large pieces of curly leaf spinach as my "bun". I also used less seasoned salt (maybe a scant teaspoon) and didn't salt during cooking. My handy dandy George Foreman grilled them very nicely, and they turned out DELICIOUS. I think next time I will increase the pesto because I love that flavor.

These are delicious! I had to make my own basil pesto because I didn't have any, but I think that made the burgers even better. Just mix the below ingredients in a food processor. 3/4 cup fresh basil leaves 1/4 cup grated Parmesan cheese 1/4 cup extra virgin olive oil 1/3 cup pine nuts or walnuts 3 medium sized garlic cloves, minced

These were fabulous- everyone in the house LOVED em. I would suggest cutting down on the amount of breadcrumbs (I used about 2 TBSP), unless your going for a "meatloaf" type of burger. Added chopped spinach, red bell pepper & made mini patties on my panini press. Served as a lettuce wrap on bibb lettuce. DIVINE!!
PLEASE NOTE: These burgers are not meant to serve with your typical mustard & ketchup toppings. If you eat them that way, please don't give them a bad review b/c they taste weird!

So yummy! I made garlic basil pesto to use for this recipe but forgot to get feta cheese. I followed the rest of the recipe exactly and it came out perfect. next time I'll be sure to use feta or maybe cheddar cheese. It seemed I did have to grill the burgers a little longer than 5 minutes each side, maybe about 8 minutes. But I used a meat thermometer to read inside meat temp until it reached about 170 degrees. This recipe is a keeper!
The BESTTurkey burgers hands down! Made as directed except no extra season salt while cooking. Do th overcook 5-8 minutes per side. No grill? Frying pan great too. Entire family loves them.

With a few changes, this is one of my favorite recipes and easy go to. I use parmesan cheese instead of feta and Italian seasoned breadcrumbs instead of plain, then omit the seasoning salt. I add pesto to mayo for a yummy sandwich spread and a tomato slice. Perfect! I've also used this recipe to make meatballs, baked in the oven. Sooo good!

Such a great new way to have Turkey burgers! I mostly followed the recipe (adding a little it of Brags liquid amino acid for flavoring). In half of the patties, I stuffed a sun dried tomato. Having that on the bun with cucumber and spinach leaves was great! Will make again!

I just happened to have all the ingredients for this recipe. We happened to have mesclun greens and cherry tomatoes from our garden, so I laid the burger on a bed of greens, topped it with cherry tomatoes and pearl mozzarella marinated in a bit of evoo, garlic paste, and basil paste, and drizzled a basalmic vinegar and honey reduction over the whole thing. It was delicious! My husband raved about it. We had leftovers tonight and it was just as good the second time. Definitely a keeper!
The feta cheese is so wrong. By the time I tweaked it it could not be called the same recipe. I mixed parmesan cheese in meat mixture and served with a creamy pesto sauce and provolone cheese.

We thought these were good. Beef burgers are our preference, but these were very flavorful. I didn't bother sprinkling extra seasoning salt on the patties as 1 1/2 teaspoons was already plenty. Topped with provolone cheese and all the fixings, these were a great weekday dinner.

I, unfortunately, used half 99% lean turkey and half 93% turkey. My goal was to make it more healthy. This made it, I think, a little less juicy. I also didn't serve it with a tomato on the bun. Lastly, I made 1/3 lb patties. Although I didn't overcook it on the grill, I would've been able to reduce the grill time with smaller 1/4 lb patties. I will probably try it again with those changes. The many flavors were positive...
This recipe is a house favorite. We add a pesto aioli on top and call them zombie burgers to get the kids to eat them!
I've made this several times, and I love how it tastes. But I can't get it to not fall apart!
I don’t like Feta cheese so i sub grated Romano. Baked at 400* about 10 min and then broiled to brown.
Great recipe. Delicious. Made in my Air Fryer for 14 min at 380 degrees for 14min.
